newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine official's murder acquittal uproar.
newsitem.headline: Philippine official's murder acquittal uproar.

text.p: Supporters of a Philippine mayor cheered and relatives of the man he was acquitted of killing slammed the justice system after a court on Tuesday cleared the politician of murder charges.
"Justice is rotten," sobbed the mother of the deceased as backers of San Ildefonso Mayor Honorato Galvez raised his arm in triumph after the judge's verdict was read in the packed court.

In a murder trial that has gripped the country, the court acquitted Galvez of charges of ordering and taking part in the 1993 killing of Alvin Vinculado, 22, and the shooting and wounding of Vinculado's twin brother and an uncle.
A driver of the mayor testified that he alone shot the three victims. He was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment.

The killing in San Ildefonso, just north of Manila, occurred during a quarrel over the mayor's order to cut down coconut trees on the Vinculado family's land to clear the way for a road widening project.
Shooting broke out when the twins and their uncle confronted the mayor, according to trial records.
The judge said the prosecution failed to present enough evidence to convict Galvez.
The case triggered a national debate because of widespread perceptions in the Philippines that the country's elite are beyond the reach of the law.
Other recent cases involve a congressman accused of sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in his Manila condominum and another mayor accused of raping a teenage student.
"We no longer have faith in the government. Life in this country is cheap," Lauro Vizconde, a member of the Crusade Against Violence, shouted as he left the court room.
The Crusade is composed of people who have been victims of criminal violence and who say they did not receive justice from the courts.
